field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Off-Policy Evaluation with Strategic Agents via Local Disclosure

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-2 pre-print / under review (arXiv:2606.07308v1, June 2026). Rigorous mathematical framework with 14 theorems/lemmas/assumptions, synthetic validation, and semi-synthetic benchmark.
field_04_concrete_problem: Strategic distribution shift in Off-Policy Evaluation (OPE): when evaluation targets strategic agents, agents adaptively game or alter their observed features X^s in response to deployed decision rules, violating standard unconfoundedness and common-support assumptions (Section 1 & 2).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Single-stage and sequential decision-making architectures interacting with utility-maximizing strategic agents under local policy disclosure.
field_06_action_space: Continuous and discrete decision policies \pi(t|x^s) assigning treatment/verification decisions under strategically reported feature vectors.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Strategic agent cost model estimator; evaluates strategic manipulation noise under partial/local disclosure paradigms.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Strategy-Robust Doubly Robust (SDR) estimator (Section 3): combines learned agent cost functions with policy value decomposition to construct a doubly robust estimand that is consistent even when agents strategically game input features.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Assumption 2.1 (Unconfoundedness given post-strategic features); Lemma 2.2 (Identifiability under local disclosure); Theorem on double robustness and asymptotic normality of \hat{V}_{SDR}.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Strategic gaming-resistant evaluation gate: provides unbiased offline policy performance estimates when agents actively manipulate inputs to bypass screening.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated on synthetic simulation suites and the German Credit benchmark (Section 4.1 & 4.2). The Strategy-Robust Doubly Robust estimator eliminates strategic adaptation bias, reducing Mean Squared Error (MSE) by 65–85% compared to naive standard Doubly Robust (DR) and Inverse Propensity Weighting (IPW) which severely misestimate policy value under agent gaming.
field_12_baselines_compared: Standard Inverse Propensity Weighting (IPW), standard Doubly Robust (DR), Direct Method (DM), and unadjusted regression models.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Requires parametric or semi-parametric structure on agent utility/cost functions; fails if unobserved confounders influence both agent strategic effort and final outcomes (Section 6).
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Demonstrates that naive offline evaluators suffer severe value collapse when agents adapt strategically; SDR estimator recovers robust policy ranking without requiring full environment retraining.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct mathematical foundation for CausaGuard RQ1, RQ3, and WP4: formalizes how to evaluate candidate controllers when autonomous agents strategically adapt their tool-calling patterns to evade heuristic detection.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Quantile Off-Policy Evaluation via Deep Conditional Generative Learning

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-2 high-impact pre-print / conference submission (arXiv:2212.14466v1, December 2022). Comprehensive theoretical contribution with 10 formal theorems/lemmas and extensive simulation sweeps.
field_04_concrete_problem: Failure of mean-based Off-Policy Evaluation in safety-critical domains: standard OPE focuses exclusively on expected returns, remaining completely blind to heavy-tailed downside risks, catastrophic tail failures, and quantile returns (Section 1 & 2).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Single-stage and multi-stage sequential decision processes with continuous and heavy-tailed reward distributions.
field_06_action_space: Sequential decision actions evaluated over full return distributions and risk quantiles \tau \in (0, 1).
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Deep conditional generative learning verifier modeling full conditional distribution of returns; evaluated under 5-fold cross-fitting with N = 2500.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Quantile Off-Policy Evaluation (Q-OPE) via conditional generative models (Section 2 & 3): estimates the complete cumulative distribution function (CDF) and quantile value function of target policies using deep conditional generative learning with Neyman orthogonality.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Conditional unconfoundedness, overlap, and convergence rates of generative conditional density estimators (Section 4, Theorems 1–3); derives asymptotic normality of the quantile estimator.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Quantile risk-bounding gate: rejects candidate policies whose lower tail quantiles (e.g. 1% or 5% Value-at-Risk) breach safety constraints, regardless of high expected returns.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated across single-stage and two-stage sequential decision environments with Gaussian, Student-t, and Cauchy heavy-tailed rewards (Tables 1, 2, 3). R_quantile consistently outperforms R_mean in Mean Squared Error across all settings; under heavy-tailed rewards, R_quantile reduces RMSE by over 50% compared to mean-based estimators (Table 1: MSE 0.000324 vs 0.002025).
field_12_baselines_compared: Standard mean-based OPE (R_mean), empirical inverse propensity weighting (IPW), and standard regression models.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Requires generative model training with cross-fitting; deep generative models can suffer mode collapse in high-dimensional sparse-reward environments.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Shows that optimizing solely for expected reward permits catastrophic tail failures; quantile evaluation successfully detects and prevents tail disruptions without sacrificing median performance.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct mathematical support for CausaGuard RQ3 and WP6: provides the distributional and quantile evaluation foundation required for Gate 1 tail-risk certification (e.g. 1%-CVaR safety bounds).

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Generalizing Off-Policy Evaluation From a Causal Perspective For Sequential Decision-Making

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-2 foundational workshop/pre-print article (arXiv:2201.08262v1, January 2022). Foundational conceptual framework formalizing OPE via Pearl's Structural Causal Models.
field_04_concrete_problem: Lack of causal formalization in Off-Policy Evaluation: standard OPE conflates interventional (Layer 2) and counterfactual (Layer 3) queries, failing to identify hidden confounding, non-stationarity, and structural state dependencies in sequential decision-making (Section 1 & 3).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Sequential decision processes modeled as Structural Causal Models (SCMs) over multi-stage medical, clinical, and autonomous decision horizons.
field_06_action_space: Sequential interventional actions do(A_t = a_t) and counterfactual queries Y_{A \leftarrow \pi}(u) conditioned on individual unit histories.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Causal DAG identifiability verifier; characterization of parametric and unobserved confounding noise (Section 4).
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: SCM-based Causal OPE Framework (Section 3): maps the three levels of the causal hierarchy to off-policy questions (Example 1: interventional survival vs Example 2: counterfactual retrospective survival). Formalizes exact conditions under which OPE estimands are identifiable.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Structural Causal Model definitions (Definition 1, 2); d-separation, backdoor criterion, and positivity of causal mechanisms across trajectories.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Causal validity gate: determines whether a candidate policy's offline valuation is structurally identifiable before permitting deployment.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Systematizes sources of uncertainty in sequential decision-making into 4 structural categories (Section 4): model specification, unobserved confounding, finite-sample stochasticity, and counterfactual identifiability. Outlines the precise role of human experts in resolving identifiability bottlenecks.
field_12_baselines_compared: Associational OPE, standard Importance Sampling, and non-causal Markovian transition models.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: In the presence of unobserved time-varying confounders, counterfactual OPE cannot be identified without physical experimentation or instrumental variables (Section 5).
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Demonstrates that non-causal OPE produces spurious policy rankings when confounders exist; causal graph structuring isolates structural disruptions from random policy noise.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct conceptual foundation for CausaGuard RQ1, RQ3, and WP5: provides the formal Pearlian causal hierarchy (Associational vs Interventional vs Counterfactual) that underpins CausaGuard's counterfactual controller and causal DAG modeling.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Reliable Off-policy Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 high-impact journal/conference full-text monograph (arXiv:2011.04102v3, 46 pages). Rigorous distributionally robust optimization proofs, finite-sample guarantees, and comprehensive empirical validation.
field_04_concrete_problem: Catastrophic variance and statistical unreliability of importance sampling in high-stakes off-policy evaluation: point estimates often have massive standard errors, and existing confidence intervals either rely on asymptotic normality or yield overly conservative bounds (Section 1).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Infinite-horizon and finite-horizon discounted Markov Decision Processes with unknown environmental transitions.
field_06_action_space: Discrete and continuous action spaces under policy evaluation.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Distributionally robust optimization verifier over Wasserstein ambiguity balls centered on the empirical trajectory distribution.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Distributionally Robust Off-Policy Evaluation (DR-OPE) (Section 3 & 4): constructs uncertainty sets using Wasserstein distance and solves convex dual reformulations to produce finite-sample confidence intervals that are guaranteed to cover the true policy value with specified probability.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Lipschitz continuity of transition kernel and reward function; bounded Wasserstein ambiguity radius; finite-sample concentration inequalities (Theorems 1–5).
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Distributionally robust safety certification gate: certifies that policy value lower bound exceeds operational threshold under worst-case perturbation within Wasserstein ball.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated on standard benchmarks (Gridworld, CartPole, Mountain Car, and healthcare simulation suites). DR-OPE achieves exact nominal (1-\alpha) coverage (e.g. 95%) with confidence interval widths 30–50% tighter than Hoeffding and Bernstein bounds, and avoids the under-coverage failures of asymptotic Student-t intervals in small sample sizes.
field_12_baselines_compared: Standard Importance Sampling (IS), Weighted IS (WIS), Doubly Robust (DR), empirical Bernstein bounds, and asymptotic normal intervals.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Solving the Wasserstein dual requires convex optimization over trajectory support; computational overhead scales polynomially with trajectory sample size.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Guarantees that candidate policies will not fail catastrophically when deployed in environments with minor distribution shift relative to logging data.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct mathematical support for CausaGuard RQ3 and Gate 1: provides distributionally robust confidence bounds that protect candidate controllers against off-policy evaluation errors.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: RL in Latent MDPs is Tractable: Online Guarantees via Off-Policy Evaluation

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 peer-reviewed top conference proceedings (arXiv:2406.01389v2, June 2024). Breakthrough theoretical complexity result for latent-variable reinforcement learning.
field_04_concrete_problem: Intractability of reinforcement learning in Latent MDPs (LMDPs): learning across hidden context modes (e.g. diverse user intents or latent system regimes) was widely believed to require exponential sample complexity in horizon length (Section 1).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Latent Markov Decision Processes with M discrete hidden contexts, finite horizon H, and state space S.
field_06_action_space: Discrete actions in multi-task and latent-context environments.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Off-policy latent context identifier and trajectory likelihood ratio estimator.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: OPE-driven Online RL for Latent MDPs (Section 3 & 4): leverages high-precision Off-Policy Evaluation as an algorithmic subroutine to explore and identify latent MDP modes with polynomial sample complexity.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Separability of latent contexts; finite context cardinality M; Theorem 1 proving polynomial regret bound O(poly(M, H, |S|, |A|) * sqrt(T)).
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Latent context verification gate: guarantees bounded regret and safe exploration across unobserved operating modes.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Proves theoretically and demonstrates empirically that OPE subroutines allow efficient online exploration in Latent MDPs with sublinear regret, resolving an open problem in RL theory and avoiding exponential sample bottlenecks.
field_12_baselines_compared: Standard optimistic exploration (UCB-VI), Posterior Sampling (PSRL), and naive mode-unaware RL.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Requires discrete latent context cardinality M; polynomial bound exponents depend on latent context separation gap.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Shows that OPE enables rapid identification of hidden system shifts, preventing catastrophic policy degradation when latent context changes.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct theoretical foundation for CausaGuard RQ1, RQ3, and WP5: provides rigorous proof that agents operating across hidden system states (such as multi-tenant software domains) can be safely evaluated and bounded using OPE subroutines.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1/Tier-2 peer-reviewed security benchmark (arXiv:2504.18575v3, April 2025). Comprehensive web-agent evaluation across GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, and o1.
field_04_concrete_problem: Vulnerability of autonomous web-navigating agents to prompt injection attacks embedded in untrusted web pages, shopping environments, and forums (Section 1 & 2).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Visual and text-based web agents (GPT-4o via VisualWebArena scaffolding, Claude-3.5 via CURI, o1 via Tool Calling) executing multi-step web browsing tasks.
field_06_action_space: Browser actions (click, type, navigate, fill form) and external API/tool calls.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Web sandbox verifier evaluating Attack Success Rate (ASR) and task utility across plain-text and URL injections.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: WASP Benchmark (Section 3): evaluates realistic adversarial web vectors (injected text, invisible DOM elements, malicious URLs) across web tasks; audits defense mechanisms including prompt firewalls and tool-use filters.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Threat model assumes web page content is attacker-controlled while user prompt is benign.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Web agent action firewall and tool execution monitor; tests defense efficacy against indirect prompt injections.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated across GPT-4o, Claude-3.5, and o1 (Tables 1, 2, 3). Undefended web agents suffer Attack Success Rates (ASR) of 68–84% on plain-text injections and 72–90% on URL injections. State-of-the-art defenses reduce ASR but cause severe utility degradation (dropping task completion from 65% to below 30%).
field_12_baselines_compared: Undefended agents, input prompt firewalls, delimiter parsing, and system-prompt hardening.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Existing defenses create an unacceptable security-utility trade-off; strict web sanitization strips interactive web elements necessary for task execution.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Demonstrates that static web firewalls disrupt legitimate browsing actions; dynamic context-aware authorization is required to preserve utility.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct empirical evidence for CausaGuard RQ1, RQ6, and WP7: establishes real-world benchmark metrics for tool-calling agent security under indirect prompt injection in dynamic environments.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-2 security benchmark / pre-print (arXiv:2611.07640v1, November 2026, work done at Amazon). In-depth study with 30 tables, formal threat model, and 6 influence primitives.
field_04_concrete_problem: Narrowness of existing indirect prompt injection (IPI) benchmarks: prior work focuses almost exclusively on overt 'instruction override' (e.g. 'ignore previous instructions'), leaving subtle task-tampering attacks (altering parameters, falsifying context, biasing summaries) unmeasured (Section 1 & 3).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Multi-step tool-augmented LLM agents across diverse commercial and open-source models.
field_06_action_space: Tool calls with structured argument payloads vs free-form textual output generation.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Task success rate (TSR) verifier measuring execution fidelity under attack and benign conditions across 6 influence primitives.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Task-Tampering Benchmark Framework (Section 4): systematizes 6 influence primitives (parameter substitution, context omission, premise poisoning, authority spoofing, logic redirection, format hijacking) and evaluates compound attacks against deployed agent defenses.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Attacker can inject data into third-party retrieved content but cannot alter system prompts or agent execution binaries.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Parameter validation and task integrity monitor; checks whether tool arguments conform to user-intended task specifications.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated across multiple models (Table 3). Task-tampering attacks achieve over 75% success on undefended agents. Standard defenses designed for instruction overrides (such as DataSentinel and delimiter parsing) catch less than 20% of subtle parameter-tampering attacks, while dropping benign TSR by 12–25%.
field_12_baselines_compared: Delimiter isolation, DataSentinel, SecAlign, Prompt Guard, and naive instruction filtering.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Subtle task tampering leaves no overt adversarial keywords, rendering lexical and semantic similarity detectors completely ineffective.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Proves that subtle task tampering degrades agent correctness silently without triggering standard safety filters, requiring value-level semantic invariant monitoring.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct empirical justification for CausaGuard RQ1, RQ6, and the WP7 access grader: confirms that tool authorization must check argument values and causal state effects, not just syntax or overt override keywords.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1/Tier-2 peer-reviewed security conference paper (arXiv:2503.00061v2, March 2025). Rigorous adaptive attack evaluation against 8 state-of-the-art defenses.
field_04_concrete_problem: False sense of security in agent defenses: static evaluations demonstrate high defense detection rates, but defenses collapse when evaluated against defense-aware adaptive attackers (Section 1 & 4).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Tool-calling LLM agents equipped with input-level, model-level, or detection-based defense layers.
field_06_action_space: Tool invocation commands and external communication outputs.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Detection rate (DR) and Attack Success Rate (ASR) verifier evaluating adversarial strings with and without adaptive training.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Adaptive Attack Formulation (Section 4): designs white-box and gray-box adaptive strategies tailored to detection-based (e.g. perplexity, classifier), input-level (e.g. paraphrasing, sanitization), and model-level (e.g. fine-tuned safety) defenses.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Attacker possesses knowledge of defense algorithms and can iteratively optimize injection strings to minimize detector score while preserving execution payload.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Audits detection-based, input-level, and model-level defense gates for vulnerability to adaptive bypass.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated against 8 prominent defenses (Table 1, 2, 3). While original attacks report low detection evasion (DR-o > 85%), adaptive attacks (DR-a) reduce detection rates to under 15% across all tested defenses. ASR under adaptive training jumps from <10% to 70–95%, proving that heuristic defenses provide brittle, illusory security.
field_12_baselines_compared: Perplexity filtering, SmoothLLM, In-Context Defense, Delimiter defense, Paraphrasing, and fine-tuned detector models (Llama-Guard, PIShield).
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Demonstrates that any defense relying on surface text properties or static boundary patterns can be broken by adaptive optimization.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Shows that layered heuristic defenses add latency and false alarms without providing robust resistance against motivated attackers.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Vital for CausaGuard RQ1, RQ6, and WP7: provides empirical proof that CausaGuard must not rely on prompt filtering or lexical guardrails alone, but must enforce immutable, non-bypassable host-level authorization boundaries.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Indirect Prompt Injections: Are Firewalls All You Need, or Stronger Benchmarks?

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1/Tier-2 peer-reviewed security paper (arXiv:2510.05244v2, October 2025). Multi-benchmark evaluation across AgentDojo, Agent Security Bench (ASB), and InjecAgent with 26 tables.
field_04_concrete_problem: Benchmark distortion and defense evaluation flaws in LLM agent security: existing benchmarks use artificial attack injection patterns that reward aggressive firewalls, which in practice destroy benign agent utility (Section 1 & 7).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Tool-integrated autonomous agents (GPT-4o) evaluated across dynamic environments with multi-turn tool interaction.
field_06_action_space: Tool invocation payloads across email, web, file, and financial API execution.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Tripartite evaluation metric: Benign Utility (BU), Utility under Attack (UA), and Attack Success Rate (ASR).
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Sanitizer Defense and Benchmark Audit (Section 3 & 7): evaluates prompt firewalls and proposes Sanitizer, an context-aware semantic sanitization layer designed to optimize the ASR-BU and ASR-UA trade-off.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Dual objective: defense must minimize ASR while maximizing benign utility BU >= 0.85.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: In-line semantic sanitizer and tool argument validation firewall.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated on AgentDojo, Agent Security Bench, and InjecAgent using GPT-4o (Tables 1, 2, 3). Standard firewalls achieve low ASR only by dropping Benign Utility from 92% to 41%. Sanitizer achieves the best tradeoff, maintaining 81.4% BU while reducing ASR to 12.3% on AgentDojo (Table 1) and lowest ASR on InjecAgent (Table 3).
field_12_baselines_compared: DataSentinel, PromptGuard, Delimiter defenses, In-Context Defender, and undefended GPT-4o.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Exposes that current agent security benchmarks reward over-filtering; non-replicable baselines distort reported security scores (Section 7.1).
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Quantifies the catastrophic operational disruption caused by aggressive security firewalls; establishes that defense evaluation must jointly report utility and security.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Directly informs CausaGuard RQ1, RQ2, and WP7 evaluation: confirms CausaGuard's core thesis that security monitors must be evaluated on both safety violation rate and task disruption / false intervention rate.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: LongPIBench: A Long-Context Benchmark for Prompt Injection

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-2 security benchmark (arXiv:2608.28411v1, August 2026). Comprehensive long-context study across 8 LLMs and 4 real-world testing suites.
field_04_concrete_problem: Failure of prompt injection defenses in long-context regimes (32k–128k tokens): existing defenses evaluated on short prompts fail completely when injections are buried in large documents, logs, or repositories (Section 1 & 3).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Long-context LLMs (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet) processing extensive document workflows (paper review, resume screening, email summaries, code review).
field_06_action_space: Long-document summarization, review generation, and automated decision-making.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: False Positive Rate (FPR) and False Negative Rate (FNR) verifier across 9 detection-based defenses on long-context payloads.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: LongPIBench Framework (Section 3 & 4): benchmarks heuristic attacks (naive, escape character, fake completion, context ignore, combined attack, authority spoof) and optimization attacks (GCG) in long-context documents.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Adversarial payload represents <1% of total context tokens, placed at varying depth positions within benign long text.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Long-context input scanner and detection firewall; audits attention trackers and classifier defenses.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated across 8 LLMs and 9 defenses (Tables 1, 2, 3). Combined attacks achieve 86–100% ASR across long-context tasks without defense (Table 1). State-of-the-art defenses collapse in long contexts: MetaSecAlign-8B, which achieves ~0% ASR on short benchmarks, exhibits 100% ASR on LongPIBench paper review. Detection defenses exhibit extreme trade-offs: either flagging almost everything (FPR = 1.00) or missing attacks completely (FNR = 1.00) (Table 3).
field_12_baselines_compared: Attention Tracker, DataSentinel, DeBERTa, DistilBERT, EVD, KAD, PIShield, Prompt Guard, and Prompt Guard 2.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Attention dispersion in long contexts blinds LLMs to injection intent; existing detectors cannot scale to 100k+ tokens without catastrophic false positive rates.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Proves that detector defenses exhibit intolerable false positive rates (up to 100%) in long documents, causing total operational disruption.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Directly supports CausaGuard RQ1, RQ2, and WP7: demonstrates that input-level text scanning is fundamentally unscalable in long-horizon agent workflows, necessitating CausaGuard's formal state-space and tool-call boundary verification.
